_comment: guard-fire-needles.json — the deny/warn text each registered hook prints, keyed by
the hook's own words rather than its filename (mantahostels#1246). Why the filename does not
work, and what a fire-shaped span is: scripts/lib/guard-fires.js.
`text` is a literal substring, or an array of substrings ALL of which must be
present in the same span — used where one clause alone is ambiguous.
Pick that substring from the fragment's OPENING sentence — `A PUSH WARNS
UNLESS FULL OR ADMISSIBLE`. Where the opening sentence is NOT the
distinctive one, key on the clause that is.
A GENERATED fragment carries its source region's Markdown (mantahostels#2528), so skip a leading
`**` emphasis marker. And it may have no sentence at all —
takes-value-vocabulary.txt is a table rendered out of docs/agents/triage-labels.md.
Key on the most distinctive verbatim CELL, never the header row, whose text recurs
in that document's other tables. REJECTED (mantahostels#2547): having
scripts/generate-rule-fragments.js emit an id headline at the head of every
fragment — it restores the convention everywhere but spends bytes on every
gp_rule-reachable id, rationed by scripts/check-context-budget.js.
count-guard-fires.test.ts asserts fragment.includes(text) ONLY for an id on a literal
`gp_rule ` line in a .sh guard, with a string `text`. One handed over any other way is
unasserted and goes stale silently.
`routes` on a NEEDLE narrows the subject's own routes, which are `hook` and
`deny` for every guard. A guard that reprints an injected fragment inside its
deny needs `routes: ["hook"]` on the injection needle, or one deny is counted
as two fires (mantahostels#2118).
`unless` on a needle lists literals only ANOTHER guard prints beside the
needle's text; a span carrying any of them is not this needle's fire. Two
guards printing one rule fragment need it, or one deny counts under both (#1759).
`needles: []` with a `silent` note is a hook that prints nothing a reader ever sees.
`kind` is documentation only — nothing reads it. Its value set: `deny` (the
tool call is refused), `warn` (additionalContext on the call that tripped it),
`notice` (a report with no call to trip — SessionStart, Stop, PostToolUse or
UserPromptSubmit), `block` (a Stop hook refusing the turn) and `inject` (a
docs/agents/rules/*.txt fragment handed over by gp_rule BEFORE any mistake,
never in response to one — mantahostels#2118, mantahostels#2136).
EVERY KEY HERE MUST NAME A REGISTRATION IN self-plugin/hooks/hooks.json AND EVERY
REGISTRATION MUST HAVE A KEY — asserted by count-guard-fires.test.ts.
